headline: The U.S. Army has announced that it has awarded Hanwha Defense USA, the American subsidiary of South Korean Hanwha Group, a contract to procure an initial batch of K9MH 155mm/52-caliber self-propelled howitzers on a wheeled chassis under the Mobile Tactical Cannon (MTC) program. The K9MH uses a Tatra 8×8 wheeled chassis. The MTC program calls for the eventual procurement of a new 155mm/52-caliber wheeled self-propelled howitzer to replace the U.S. Army’s 155mm/39-caliber M777A2 lightweight towed howitzers. The contract with Hanwha Defense USA covers the delivery of six K9MH prototypes to the U.S. Army for $100.3 million, with an option for an additional 12 prototypes. If the option is exercised, the total contract value could increase to $262.9 million. The K9MH howitzers will be used in a four-year evaluation and testing phase. In addition to Hanwha Defense USA’s K9MH, other 155mm/52-caliber wheeled self-propelled howitzers competing under the MTC program include the SIGMA, proposed by a consortium of Elbit America, Anduril, and Oshkosh Defense; the CAESAR, proposed by Leonardo DRS and KNDS; the RCH 155 from Rheinmetall; and the Archer from BAE Systems. Hanwha is proposing to produce the K9MH for the U.S. Army at its new facility currently under construction in Opelika, Alabama. However, despite the K9MH’s formal selection under the MTC program, it is by no means certain that the system will ultimately enter U.S. Army service.
summary: The U.S. Army has announced that it has awarded Hanwha Defense USA, the American subsidiary of South Korean Hanwha Group, a contract to procure an initial batch of K9MH 155mm/52-caliber self-propelled howitzers on a wheeled chassis under the Mobile Tactical Cannon (MTC) program.

headline: For those who want to understand Iran after the war, they should listen to the interview with Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council. Rezaei outlined Tehran’s approach and its relations with its neighbors, as well as its view of Washington. He spoke openly so that no one would be caught off guard by any future move, and dismissed concerns over neighborly relations that the Iranians believe have harmed their national security. Rezaei’s interview suggests that Tehran has freed itself from the “excessive restraint” that created an opening through which Washington was able to infiltrate and wage a prolonged war, while pushing some of Iran’s neighbors to provide facilities and assistance, willingly or otherwise. The factor of “power” will be a cornerstone of Iran’s dealings with the outside world, not as an act of aggression, but to establish red lines that it will not allow to be crossed. This would also close the door to policies of circumvention and excuses based on “American pressure.” Accordingly, Tehran’s new policy holds that anyone who takes an action must bear responsibility for it. Tehran believes it has succeeded in changing the rules of the game in the region and weakening the U.S. presence there, the full extent of which will become clearer later. It therefore believes that it is now necessary to act according to the new realities it has established, which cannot be ignored. Its view of the emerging alliances is not hostile, but at the same time, it does not support them. Rather, Tehran believes in building an alliance that includes everyone, in accordance with the changes taking place in the region. Rezaei described these changes as the gains achieved by the Iranian people, and therefore something they have a right to.

headline: The Chief of Staff of Iran’s Armed Forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi, visited one of Iran’s underground facilities involved in the production of ballistic missiles. The visit is a clear message to those claiming that Iran is no longer capable of producing ballistic missiles, particularly solid-fuel systems. What has been destroyed on the surface is nothing compared to what remains underground. I spoke with several people from Iranian military circles, and they confirmed to me that pre-war munitions are still stockpiled in quantities sufficient to last for years. This means reports based on “intelligence” estimates of Iran’s remaining ballistic missile inventory should be taken with caution, as they are often based on very limited information. Thousands upon thousands of ballistic missiles are still stockpiled. On top of that, production has increased significantly, while upgrades are constantly being made to improve the accuracy and overall performance of the missiles. As for the drones, one person put it simply: “We have drones that can go for centuries.” That doesn’t mean everything is fine or that Iran has no problems. There are shortages of trained ballistic missile operators, and recruitment has already started. The reason is obvious: not everyone can be selected to join the IRGC Aerospace Force, as there are specific criteria that candidates have to meet.

headline: Nearly six months after the Navy evacuated about 1,300 family members from Bahrain, the service is telling them they should not expect to return anytime soon according to reporting from Stars & Stripes. The prolonged evacuation has exposed major gaps in the military's relocation system. Families report tens of thousands of dollars in unreimbursed expenses, stranded vehicles and household goods, repeated moves, and uncertainty over housing, schools and medical care. Vice Adm. Curt Renshaw, commander of U.S. Naval Forces Central Command, acknowledged the problem directly, telling evacuees: “We literally have been making this up as we go, because nothing is conceived to go on this length of time.” The Navy is now directing dependents to designate a new permanent duty station, generally in the U.S, where their belongings can be delivered and they can transition out of temporary safe haven status. They could potentially return if conditions improve. Source: https://www.stripes.com/branches/navy/2026-08-21/bahrain-evacuation-military-families-navy-22618186.html

headline: The U.S. Navy has publicly disclosed a previously unannounced AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missile (LRAAM), also known as the "Malice", revealing the weapon mounted inside the internal weapons bay of an F-35C Lightning II with an AIM-120 AMRAAM mounted on the bay door. The Navy describes the AIM-424 as its next-generation, long range air to air missile, intended to give Navy and Marine Corps aviators greater capability against advanced threats. The internal carriage is particularly significant. Rather than simply adding another externally carried long-range missile, the AIM-424 appears to have been designed around the F-35's limited internal weapons-bay dimensions, allowing the aircraft to retain its low-observable configuration while carrying a substantially longer-range air-to-air weapon. The missile is still associated with testing and development, and the Navy has released few technical details regarding its range, seeker, propulsion or intended employment. The available imagery does, however, show the AIM-424 being evaluated on both the F-35C and F/A-18E/F, indicating that the weapon is being considered across the Navy's carrier aviation force. headline: The USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) has left the Middle East after 274 days deployed, with the carrier strike group now operating in the Indian Ocean under U.S. 7th Fleet, according to USNI. The carrier departed San Diego on Nov. 25 and has been at sea since its last port visit in Guam on Dec. 11—more than eight months without a port call, breaking the previous 206-day record set by USS Dwight D. Eisenhower during the COVID-19 pandemic. The unusually long deployment was compounded by the loss of regional logistics hubs following Iranian attacks, forcing Navy supply ships to travel thousands of miles to sustain the carrier and other forces operating in the Arabian Sea. The Navy says resupply problems improved after new supply lines were established. Lincoln is being replaced in the region by the forward deployed USS George Washington (CVN-73), which arrived two days ago and will join USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77) to maintain a two carrier presence amid the war with Iran. From the Western Indian Ocean, it will take Lincoln 3-4 weeks to transit across the Pacific back to San Diego. An open question is whether the ship will make a port call on the way home, which would extend the deployment a few days. The Navy is now dealing with a broader pattern of extended deployments: USNI notes that carrier deployments since October 2023 have averaged about 8½ months, while USS Gerald R. Ford recently completed a record 326-day deployment. Source: https://news.usni.org/2026/08/22/uss-abraham-lincoln-leaves-the-middle-east-after-almost-7-months

headline: According to the Wall Street Journal, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is expected to leave his post by the end of the year, or possibly sooner, after months of reported tension with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. Driscoll has served about 18 months and developed a close working relationship with former Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George. The two pushed the Army toward greater use of commercial technology and lessons from Ukraine, including integrating commercially available systems more rapidly into military operations. George was abruptly fired by Hegseth in April and has not been replaced by a Senate-confirmed successor. Gen. Christopher LaNeve is currently serving as acting Army chief of staff. Driscoll's departure would therefore leave both of the Army's top civilian and uniformed leadership positions without Senate-confirmed permanent leaders. The reported split also appears to reflect a broader disagreement over Army transformation. Driscoll had advocated adopting Ukrainian style approaches to commercial technology and battlefield innovation, while his relationship with Hegseth reportedly deteriorated after Driscoll became involved in efforts to arrange senior level visits and Army reform discussions. There has been no official confirmation of Driscoll's departure. The Pentagon and Driscoll's representatives declined to comment. Source: https://www.wsj.com/politics/national-security/army-secretary-expected-to-step-down-by-years-end-d7477efb

headline: Federal prosecutors say an Albany, New York, woman was arrested after allegedly developing a plan to attack the New York State Capitol and kill state senators in the name of ISIS. According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of New York, Jessica Bowie, 35, was arrested Aug. 19 after taking possession of what she believed was an explosive device. Investigators allege she had sworn allegiance to ISIS, photographed the Capitol and discussed destroying the building, killing lawmakers and disrupting the U.S. government. The complaint also alleges Bowie expressed support for al-Qaeda's 9/11 attacks online, threatened to poison Americans and recorded and distributed a formal bay'ah, or oath of allegiance, to ISIS. Prosecutors say the alleged plan went beyond rhetoric: investigators allege Bowie intended to attack the Capitol and then flee to join ISIS controlled territory. The device she obtained was apparently part of the FBI's effort to identify and disrupt the alleged plot before an attack could occur. Bowie was charged with attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization, a federal offense carrying a maximum sentence of 20 years. She was ordered detained pending further proceedings.

headline: The FBI has raided former Rep. Eric Swalwell’s Washington home and seized electronic devices at San Francisco airport as part of a federal investigation into sexual assault allegations against him. The raid comes after Swalwell resigned from Congress and ended his campaign for governor of California in April following multiple allegations of sexual misconduct. The Manhattan DA and Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department are also investigating. Swalwell was previously linked to Christine Fang, or “Fang Fang,” a Chinese national investigated by the FBI as a suspected Chinese intelligence operative who had cultivated relationships with politically promising Bay Area politicians. Newly released FBI documents reportedly show Swalwell acknowledged having a sexual relationship with Fang between 2012 and 2015. Swalwell was briefed by U.S. intelligence about concerns surrounding Fang, cut off contact with her and cooperated with the FBI. He was never charged with wrongdoing, and the House Ethics Committee ultimately closed its investigation without action. Swalwell has denied the sexual-assault allegations.

headline: Another day of heightened aerial activity near the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Thanks to reporting from @thewarzonewire's @Haltman, we now know the activity is part of a U.S.-led NATO exercise that also includes a ground component involving Polish armed forces, although their specific role has not been disclosed. Several U.S. Air Force and NATO tankers are operating in refueling racetrack orbits over Polish airspace, while a NATO E-3 AWACS is orbiting just north of the tanker tracks. A U.S. Air Force EA-37B "Compass Call II" electronic-warfare aircraft has also made the trip into the area again, this time flying directly from Chania, Greece, before operating near Kaliningrad. A NATO official told The War Zone that the exercise is not in response to recent Russian military activity or rhetoric. However, comments from a Polish official appeared to indicate that deterrence is part of the broader purpose of the exercise. The activity remains notable given the concentration of airborne early warning, electronic warfare, ISR and aerial refueling capabilities operating in close proximity to Kaliningrad.

headline: The Air Force has now placed Maj. Jason Watson in pretrial confinement following his public calls for President Donald J. Trump’s impeachment. Watson was previously arrested on July 1st after delivering a speech on the U.S. Capitol steps calling for the impeachment of President Trump while in uniform. He was not formally charged by the military over that demonstration, although wearing a uniform while participating in political activity is prohibited by military regulations. He was detained again on Aug. 18, one day after criticizing Trump in a CNN interview. According to his attorney, Watson had informed his chain of command that he would no longer wear his uniform and was arrested after refusing an order to put it back on. The Air Force says there is probable cause supporting allegations of “continued misconduct,” but Watson has not yet been formally charged. His attorney expects potential charges under Article 88, which prohibits contemptuous words against certain senior government officials, or Article 92 for failure to obey an order. Source: https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/19/politics/us-airman-arrested-at-capitol-trump-impeachment-detained
